newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN says pace of Albanian refugee exodus picks up.
newsitem.headline: UN says pace of Albanian refugee exodus picks up.

text.p: More than 2,500 Albanians fled armed unrest in their Balkan homeland for Italy on Tuesday and the pace of their exodus is picking up, the United Nations refugee agency UNHCR said.

Spokeswoman Maki Shinohara said Italy and Greece had so far received nearly 12,000 refugees from Albania, which plunged into chaos after the collapse of fraudulent get-rich-quick schemes impoverished thousands of families and roused stormy anti-government protests.
"Right now, we're seeing increasing numbers of refugees day after day," she said. The rate of departures had doubled to more than 2,000 refugees a day this week, she added.
The UNHCR was concerned about the fate of refugees on decrepit, overloaded ships sailing from Albania in the choppy waters of the Adriatic Sea.
U.S. Navy forces in the Adriatic picked up 85 Albanians from two stricken boats on Sunday, including one that capsized with 55 men on board, who were rescued by U.S. sailors.
Some 8,000 Albanians have fled to Italy in recent days in a ramshackle flotilla of rusting boats. Recent arrivals said they paid racketeers in the port of Durres for a passage to Italy.

Earlier, spokeswoman Pamela O'Toole said the UNHCR was worried about unaccompanied children including a four-month-old baby found on a ship bound for Italy. Military deserters and those without papers were also of concern.
The agency has urged Italy and Greece to give the Albanians temporary asylum and register them.
O'Toole said 120 boats carrying Albanians had arrived so far in Italy, where authorities had also registered 342 military men.
Italy was hit by an exodus of tens of thousands of Albanians in 1991 after communist rule crumbled. It has said it will grant refugees only temporary sanctuary.
